title: Marsdoku: an AI-assisted browser puzzle with 72 boards checked by an independent solver
author: Silly-Speech1514
selftext:
We’re House of Founders BV, the makers of Marsdoku, a free browser logic puzzle in a fictional Mars setting: [https://marsdoku.com/](https://marsdoku.com/)



The project uses AI-assisted coding, ImageGen for terrain and plant artwork, and ElevenLabs-generated narration. The game itself runs in vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript.



The development detail that matters most here is checking the rules separately from the presentation. The 72-board collection has behavioral checks against an independent runtime solver, including connected regions and unique solutions. That gives the visual work a fixed gameplay target: one sapling per row, column and colored region, with no two touching even diagonally.



Input behavior has its own checks too. A single tap toggles a note; a rapid double-tap confirms a sapling. Undo changes notes without refunding mistakes or removing discoveries. Save/reload behavior is checked separately, because a board looking correct doesn’t establish that progress survives a reload. Progress stays local to the browser, rather than syncing between devices.



This is a small finished game with an interactive tutorial, playable on desktop and mobile without an account or download. We’d welcome feedback on the tutorial and on the single-tap/double-tap distinction. For other AI-assisted puzzle developers, how do you keep your board validation independent of the code that renders and plays it?
